question.problem: A programmer reviews his web page and notices that, on average, $7$ visitors view his page every minute. What is the probability that there will be $5$ visitors in the next minute? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that visitors connect to the site independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of visitors to the web page. Since the average rate is $7$ visitors per minute, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of visitors can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =7,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(7).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{7}^{x}{e}^{-7}}{x!}
$$

Therefore, the probability of having $5$ visitors in the next minute is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=5) & =f(5) \\  & =\frac{{7}^{5}{e}^{-7}}{5!} \\  & ≈0.128\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
